Subject: Private deploy questionnaire — operator separation and audit artifacts

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the tabletop earlier. As part of our procurement packet we're consolidating technical evidence on operator separation for VPC/on-prem installs. Two quick asks so we can move the RFP to our architecture review: 

1) A short evidence matrix showing control owners for operator activities (deploy, patch, credential management, telemetry access) and which artifacts you can provide for audit (screenshots, runbook excerpts, attestation letters).
2) Clarification on logical vs. physical operator separation in a Private deployment — specifically: can you demonstrate a documented operator role boundary and an audit trail proving operator actions are limited to customer-scoped resources?

We'd appreciate any attachments you can provide; a brief timeline for delivery would be helpful as we have a Dec 8th compliance gate.

Thanks,
Julia

LumenHealth

Subject: Re: Private deploy questionnaire — operator separation and audit artifacts

Hi Julia,

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached an initial evidence matrix and a short narrative addressing logical vs physical operator separation for our Private (VPC/on-prem) offering. High level answers up front:

- We enforce customer-scoped operator boundaries via RBAC + network tenancy. Operators authenticate to a customer-managed bastion or jump host in customer VPC for on-prem installs; on Redwood-managed Dedicated hardware we use project-level isolation + audited operator sessions.
- Audit trail: every operator action that touches customer infrastructure or runtime is logged in the tenant's audit channel (syslog/forward to customer SIEM) and we can produce runbook excerpts and session export artifacts for audit.

Deliverables attached now: 'initial-evidence-matrix.xlsx' (matrix + availability), and 'operator-boundary-diagram.pdf' (logical diagram). I'm looping in Irene (ops) to provide the operator runbook excerpt and a sample session export.

We can provide signed attestation for deployment procedures on request — target turnaround 3 business days once you confirm the specific artifacts you need.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

[Attachments: initial-evidence-matrix.xlsx (XLSX), operator-boundary-diagram.pdf (PDF)]

Hi Julia,

Following up with the technical artifacts you asked for. Please find the excerpts and a short explanation below. I've included stubbed examples rather than production session logs for privacy, but these are representative of what we will export for audit.

1) Operator role mapping (excerpt):
- Operator: infra-operator (internal) — permissions: node lifecycle, kernel/driver upgrades restricted to non-customer shared infra; does NOT have access to customer data volumes or model keys.
- Operator: tenant-admin (customer or delegated) — permissions: runtime start/stop in customer project only.

2) Runbook excerpt for patch workflow:
- Step 1: Preflight: generate patch plan and notify customer via ops channel.
- Step 2: Acquire approval token (MFA + signed PR) recorded to audit log.
- Step 3: Apply patch to staging pool; collect metrics; promote to customer pool if green.

3) Session export example (anonymized):
- On 2026-11-18T14:02:01Z — operator session started; command: /usr/local/bin/restart-runtime --project=lumencare-prod; approval_token=tok-***; session_id=sess-9fa3.

4) Evidence we can provide for audit: runbook excerpts (txt), anonymized session exports (json/csv), role-to-policy mapping (IAM policies), and signed attestation letter. We can also forward tenant audit logs to your SIEM via TLS syslog or S3 bucket delivery.

Attachments included here: 'operator-runbook-excerpt.txt' (excerpt), 'session-export-sample.json' (anonymized).

If you'd like, Marissa can provide a short architecture note on how network tenancy enforces lateral isolation; looping her in.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Operations
irene_choi@redwood.ai

[Attachments: operator-runbook-excerpt.txt (TXT), session-export-sample.json (JSON)]

Hi Julia — quick architecture note to clarify the isolation model:

- For VPC/on-prem installs we rely on tenant network segmentation plus host-level namespaces. Operator tools run from an ops jump host that sits in a separate management VPC/subnet; connections to customer resources require per-project credentials and a short-lived session token issued after a documented approval flow.
- Physical separation: for air-gapped or high-assurance customers we can deploy operators only on console machines inside the customer boundary (operator console image), and we deliver signed runbooks and on-site operator attestation if required.

We will upload the architecture note and a sample policy bundle to the shared drive folder (link below). Let us know if you want an encrypted bundle delivered to your GLA (GovLinkAccess) mailbox.
